look_here_first: Look at the overall frond architecture: pinnae spread in a broad, fanlike or horseshoe arrangement from the upper end of a slender dark stipe. Contrast this with the elongated, repeatedly branching triangular fronds of the locally relevant Adiantum capillus-veneris; do not identify by black stalk alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Terrestrial rhizomatous perennial fern, not a flowering plant.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Slender glossy dark brown to black stipe; pinnae radiate or curve in a fanlike arrangement from the distal stipe.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Small asymmetrical fan- to wedge-shaped pinnules with repeatedly forked veins.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fertile pinnule margins roll back to form false indusia over marginal sori.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Spore-bearing structures, not flowers or seeds, are the reproductive characters to inspect.

lookalikes.differences: Frond branching pattern first; then fertile pinnule margins and pinna arrangement.
